scenes.title: The Voyage to the Land of the Dead
scenes.summary: Odysseus' tale goes on. They launch the ship with the sheep aboard and sail all day before the wind Circe sends, until at sunset they reach the limits of Oceanus, the land and the city of the Cimmerian men, wrapped in mist and cloud, where the Sun never looks on them. They beach the ship, take out the sheep and go along the stream of Oceanus to the place Circe pointed out.

scenes.title: The Rites at the Pit
scenes.summary: Perimedes and Eurylochus hold the victims while Odysseus digs the pit and pours the drink offering to all the dead, honey and milk, sweet wine and water, with white barley meal, and vows a barren heifer and a black sheep for Teiresias. He cuts the sheeps' throats over the pit, and the souls of the dead gather out of Erebus with a wondrous cry: brides and young men, old men, girls, and men slain in battle. Pale fear seizes him; the companions flay and burn the sheep and pray to Hades and Persephone, and he sits with his sword drawn, keeping the dead from the blood until he has questioned Teiresias.

scenes.title: Elpenor
scenes.summary: First comes the soul of Elpenor, still unburied, whom they left in Circe's house. Odysseus weeps and asks how he came to the misty darkness sooner on foot than they in the black ship. Elpenor tells how blind folly and wine brought him down from the roof, and begs Odysseus by those at home to burn him with his armor on Aeaea and heap him a tomb on the shore with his oar fixed on it. Odysseus promises.

scenes.title: Teiresias
scenes.summary: The soul of his mother Anticleia comes, whom he left alive; he weeps but will not let her near the blood before Teiresias. Then Theban Teiresias comes with his golden scepter, drinks, and prophesies: Poseidon's anger for his son; the cattle of the Sun on Thrinacia, which they must not harm; a late and evil homecoming in another's ship, the suitors in his house, and his vengeance; then a journey inland with an oar until men who know nothing of the sea call it a winnowing fan, a sacrifice to Poseidon, and a gentle death away from the sea in an old age of ease. He tells Odysseus that any of the dead he lets near the blood will speak truly, and goes back into the house of Hades.

scenes.title: Anticleia
scenes.summary: His mother drinks and knows him at once, and asks how he came alive into the darkness. He asks how she died, and of his father, his son and his wife. She tells him that Penelope still waits in tears, that Telemachus holds the domains in peace, that Laertes lives on the farm in rags, grieving, and that she herself died of longing for him. Three times he tries to embrace her and three times she flits from his hands like a shadow; she explains that this is the way of mortals when they die, and bids him go back to the light.

scenes.title: The Heroines
scenes.summary: Persephone sends the wives and daughters of chieftains, and Odysseus questions them one by one with his sword drawn: Tyro, whom Poseidon loved in the likeness of the river Enipeus, mother of Pelias and Neleus; Antiope, mother of Amphion and Zethus, the founders of Thebes; Alcmene, mother of Heracles; Megara; Epicaste, the mother who married her son Oedipus; Chloris, Neleus' queen, whose daughter Pero was to go only to the man who drove off the cattle of Iphiclus, the task a seer undertook; Leda and her sons Castor and Polydeuces, alive on alternate days; Iphimedeia and the giant sons who tried to pile Ossa on Olympus and Pelion on Ossa; Phaedra, Procris and Ariadne; Maera, Clymene and Eriphyle. He breaks off: it is time to sleep.

scenes.title: In the Hall of Alcinous
scenes.summary: The Phaeacians sit spellbound in silence. Arete praises her guest and bids the Phaeacians not to cut short his gifts; old Echeneus agrees and leaves the word to Alcinous, who promises the gifts and the escort for the next day. Odysseus answers that he would stay a year for such gifts. Alcinous says he is no deceiver, but has told his tale with a singer's skill, and asks him whether he saw any of the heroes who died at Troy: the night is long, and he could listen till dawn.

scenes.title: Agamemnon
scenes.summary: Odysseus goes on. Persephone scatters the women, and the soul of Agamemnon comes, weeping, unable to grasp Odysseus with his old strength. He tells how Aegisthus with his accursed wife killed him at a feast like an ox at the manger, his companions slaughtered around him like hogs, and how Clytemnestra would not even close his eyes and mouth; he heard Cassandra's cry as she died. He warns Odysseus against trusting wives, though Penelope is not like his own, tells him to put in to his own land in secret, and asks for news of his son Orestes, of whom Odysseus knows nothing.

scenes.title: Achilles
scenes.summary: The souls of Achilles, Patroclus, Antilochus and Ajax come. Achilles asks how Odysseus dared to come down to Hades. Odysseus calls him the most blessed of men, honored like the gods in life and mighty among the dead. Achilles answers that he would rather be bound to the soil as a hired man to a man without land than be lord of all the dead, and asks after Peleus and his son. Odysseus tells him of Neoptolemus, best in counsel and in battle at Troy, who killed Eurypylus son of Telephus, never trembled in the wooden horse, and came home unwounded with his prize; and the soul of Achilles goes off with long strides across the meadow of asphodel, glad.

scenes.title: Ajax
scenes.summary: The other souls stand grieving and ask about their sorrows; only the soul of Ajax son of Telamon stands apart, still angry for the victory over the arms of Achilles, which the sons of the Trojans and Pallas Athena judged. Odysseus wishes he had never won such a prize, and begs him to put away his anger; Ajax answers nothing and goes off into Erebus among the other souls of the dead.

scenes.title: Minos and the Punished
scenes.summary: Odysseus sees Minos, the splendid son of Zeus, giving judgment to the dead with his golden scepter; Orion herding the beasts he killed across the meadow of asphodel; Tityus, son of Earth, stretched over nine plethra while two vultures tear his liver, for he did violence to Leto; Tantalus standing in a lake, the water vanishing whenever he stoops to drink and the wind flinging the fruit up toward the clouds whenever he reaches for it; and Sisyphus heaving his huge stone up the hill, only to have it roll back to the plain.

scenes.title: Heracles
scenes.summary: Then Odysseus sees the phantom of mighty Heracles (he himself is among the gods, the husband of Hebe), with the dead scattering in terror around him like birds, his bow drawn, and the terrible baldric with its golden strap, wrought with beasts and battles and slaughter. Heracles knows him and speaks to him lamenting: he too drew out an evil fate, slave to a lesser man who set him hard labors, and once was sent down to bring back the hound of Hades, which he did with the help of Hermes and Athena.

scenes.title: The Return to the Ship
scenes.summary: Odysseus waits on, hoping to see the heroes of old, Theseus and Peirithous; but the countless tribes of the dead gather with a wondrous din, and pale fear takes him that Persephone may send the Gorgon's head from Hades. He goes back to the ship, the companions embark and loose the cables, and the wave of the stream carries the ship down the river Oceanus, first with rowing and then with a fair wind.

days.label: Night of Day 33
days.note: Odysseus' tale goes on at the evening feast in the house of Alcinous; at 11.330–332 he offers to stop for the night, and the Phaeacians and Alcinous bid him go on: the night is "very long, endless" (11.373). Within the tale, the voyage to the land of the dead takes a single day (11.11–19).
